title: Session-log ZIP entry paths are built from an unvalidated ImageAttachmentRef parsed out of the stored log
detail: `collectImageRefs` walks the raw JSONL of the exported artifact and does `refs.set(String(ref.attachmentId), ref)` with no shape validation; `mediaEntryPath` then interpolates that raw value into the archive path (`media/${String(ref.attachmentId)}.${MEDIA_TYPE_EXTENSIONS[ref.mediaType]}`) and `deps.attachments.readImage(ref)` is called with it. Session ids get `safeSessionIdSegment()` and spill names get `encodeSegment()`, but attachment ids get neither, and an `attachmentId` outside the four known media types silently yields an entry named `media/<id>.undefined`. Exploitability is low today

title: The duplication gate excludes all test code and all JS, in the loosest mode
detail: `npm run duplication` (`jscpd --config .jscpd.json packages scripts`) is a blocking gate in `ci-primary`, `ci-consumers` and `ci-windows-observational`, but the config sets `mode: "mild"` (looser than jscpd's default `strict`), `minTokens: 60` / `minLines: 6` (so a 5-line or 59-token clone is invisible), `ignore: ["**/tests/**"]` (the largest source of copy-paste in the repo), and `format: ["typescript", "tsx"]` — which drops the 36 `.mjs`/`.cjs` files and every `.js` file from the scan. `packages` and `scripts` are also the only two roots scanned, so `apps/cli/src/plugin.ts` and the `website`

title: npm publish paths use mutable action tags while sibling workflows SHA-pin the same actions
detail: The publish jobs that hold registry credentials pull third-party code from a mutable ref: `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1` at python-release.yml:211 and :246 in jobs with `id-token: write`, and `actions/checkout@v4` / `actions/setup-node@v4` / `actions/download-artifact@v4` at landlock-run-release.yml:144-154 in a job that also has `id-token: write`. The same repository SHA-pins the equivalent calls elsewhere (`actions/checkout@3d3c42e5…` in issue-policy.yml:20 and issue-lifecycle.yml:47), so the convention exists and is simply not applied to the workflows that publish. title: Patched node-pty honors CF_NODE_PTY_SPAWN_HELPER, letting env control which binary is executed as the PTY spawn helper
detail: The local patch makes node-pty's unixTerminal.js read `process.env.CF_NODE_PTY_SPAWN_HELPER` and, if set, `path.resolve()` it and use it as the spawn-helper executable — bypassing both the sibling-of-execPath fallback and the packaged `native.dir + '/spawn-helper'`. Any code able to set environment variables in the host process (another plugin, a config `!!js` expression, a wrapper script) can point this at an arbitrary executable that then runs on every PTY spawn, giving a durable code-execution/persistence hook inside the terminal subsystem. title: A misspelled launcher flag is reported as "--profile <name> is required"
detail: Because the first unknown token starts the app-argument boundary (`allowUnknownOption()` + `passThroughOptions()`, lines 127-129), a typo'd launcher flag never reaches commander's unknown-option handler (and `showSuggestionForTypo` therefore never runs). The action then reports the generic missing-profile error. Verified against the real parser: `cf --profil web`, `cf --porfile web` and `cf --unknown-global-flag` all exit 1 with `error: --profile <name> is required` — telling a user who *did* type a `--profile`-shaped flag that they omitted it, with no hint of which token was unrecognized. title: allowScripts hint misses npm's other git-host shorthands (gitlab:, bitbucket:, git://)
detail: reference/README.md promises that "Git-hosted plugins that ship sources build during install through their `prepare` script, the first `add` fails with npm's `allowScripts` hint (and a cf pointer at the profile's `package.json`)". The regex only matches `git+`, `github:`, and a `.git` URL/fragment. npm also accepts `gitlab:user/repo` and `bitbucket:user/repo` git-host shorthands and plain `git://host/repo.git` — the last is covered by `\.git(?:#|$)`, but `gitlab:`/`bitbucket:` are not, and neither is the bare `user/repo#ref` GitHub form npm resolves to git. title: A bundle resolution failure is treated as "not a bundle", silently removing it from cf.profile.bundles
detail: `exportsPatch` collapses *any* `resolveBundleDir` failure into `false` (comment: "npm reported success yet the package is unresolvable — treat as plain"). That boolean feeds both branches of `reconcilePlugins`: line 67 (`isBundle && !plugins.includes`) to add, and line 82/83 (`dependencySet.has(pkg) && !exportsPatch(pkg)`) to *remove* an existing entry. The comment only justifies the add side.
